name: Can a new tile backsplash be installed directly over existing drywall?

mainEntity.name: Can a new tile backsplash be installed directly over existing drywall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Installing a backsplash over existing drywall is standard, provided the drywall is structurally sound, clean, flat, and dry. If existing tile is removed, the drywall paper often tears or leaves gouges; these areas must be patched, skim-coated, or replaced before setting new tile. Installing tile directly over existing tile or painted, glossy walls is not recommended without proper mechanical roughing or a specialized bonding primer. If wall surfaces around sinks or cooktops have past water or grease damage, repairing the drywall first ensures the new mortar bonds securely without future hollow spots.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, as long as the drywall is clean, flat, and structurally sound. Torn or damaged drywall from previous tile removal must be repaired before installation.
